newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps rates Turkey's Ottoman Bank debt.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps rates Turkey's Ottoman Bank debt.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said it has assigned a Triple-B-Plus rating to the long-term domestic currency debt of Turkey's Ottoman Bank and a rating of D-Two to its short-term local currency debt.
D&P rated Ottoman Bank's long-term foreign currency debt Double-B-Minus, which is limited by the rating for Turkey.
The ratings incorporate Ottoman Bank's capital position and good profitability, as well as the bank's long history and strong ownership, D&P said in a statement dated April 28.
"Ottoman's performance over the past few years has been solid," it said.

D&P said Ottoman's net interest income, for example, rose 151 percent as of December 31, 1996, against net interest income growth of 44 percent in 1995. In June 1996, Ottoman was acquired by Clover Investments, a foreign unit Garanti Bank, which is owned by the Dogus Group.

"The Dogus Group intends to continue to develop Ottoman's target markets consisting of mid-size companies and middle-income individuals, as well as expanding into large corporate clients and high net worth individuals," D&P said.
At year-end 1996, Ottoman Bank's assets totaled $891 million and it was ranked the 17th largest privately held bank in Turkey in terms of total assets.
